messages.body_plain:
scan1 requires that the first argument be a "calc_genoprob" object, as output by calc_genoprob. So that'll be a list of 3-d arrays, one per chromosome, with the 3d arrays being like individuals x genotypes x positions.

The intcovar argument needs to be a numeric matrix, individuals x covariates. And the row names need to be the individual names.

The lack of the individual names is what the error message is about, but I think the problem in your code is larger than that.

I presume that "pr" is an object with genotype probabilities, and that B02 is one of the chromosomes. And then you're trying to pull out the 2nd and 363rd positions? You'd need to do pr$B02[,,2] and pr$B02[,,363]. Those should each then be matrices with individuals as rows.

But you can't use scan1 on a single position. And you wouldn't want to include all of the genotype columns as covariates; you need to drop one of them since the probabilities sum to 1.

So maybe try:

intco <- pr$B02[ , -1, 363, drop=FALSE]
output <- scan1(pr[,"B02"], pheno=RILs$pheno, kinship=kinship_loco$B02,
                intcovar=intco)

karl

messages.subject: Re: Problems running scan1snps()
messages.body_plain:
There are several problem here.

First, there are more markers in snps than there are in model.probs.tmp, but scan1snps requires that the markers in the genoprobs object matches those in the map object. So you need to subset map_3 to the markers that are actually in pr_f_doqtl.

Second, the chromosome IDs "chr1", "chr2", ..., "chrX", in model.probs.tmp and snps don't match the chromosome ID in variants_1_10_20_Mb.

Third, the positions in map_3 are in bp, which those in variants_1_10_20_Mb are in Mbp.

Finally, you need to use snpinfo=variants_1_10_20_Mb in the call to scan1snps().

I attach a modified version of your code. The 3 key changes:

1. revise the chromosome IDs and positions in snps:

    snps$chr <- sub("^chr", "", snps$chr)
    snps$pos <- snps$pos/1e6

2. subset map_3 to the markers in pr_f_doqtl:

    mar <- unlist(lapply(pr_f_doqtl, function(a) dimnames(a)[[3]]))
    map_3 <- lapply(map_3, function(a) a <- a[names(a) %in% mar])

3. change call to scan1snps to use snpinfo and not query_func:

    out_snps_f <- scan1snps(

        genoprobs = pr_f_doqtl,
        map = map_3,
        pheno = dato,

        kinship = kinship_loco_f,
        snpinfo = variants_1_10_20_Mb,
        keep_all_snps = TRUE
    )

karl

Karl,
Thank you. You were right and that explains why I was having trouble finding it in Rqtl2. I was able to make the plot in DOQTL and will just post here how to do that in case anyone else wants to make the plot:

#Use DOQTL to get SDP for association mapping.
#First convert genotype probabilities from Rqtl2 to DOQTL
library(DOQTL)
library(qtl2convert)
probs = probs_qtl2_to_doqtl(apr)

#Make new kinship matrix
#Download snps from jax website: ftp://ftp.jax.org/MUGA/GM_snps.Rdata
K = kinship.probs(probs = probs, snps = GM_snps, bychr = FALSE)

#Run association map
#Dowload snp.file from jax website: ftp://ftp.jax.org/SNPtools/variants/mgp.v5.merged.snps_all.dbSNP142.vcf.gz and ftp://ftp.jax.org/SNPtools/variants/mgp.v5.merged.snps_all.dbSNP142.vcf.gz.tbi
results = assoc.map(pheno = pheno, pheno.col = 56, probs = probs, K = K, snps = GM_snps, snp.file = "~/DO/mgp.v5.merged.snps_all.dbSNP142.vcf.gz", chr = 17, start = 34.75, end = 37.75)
# This Warning Message is okay: Warning message:In .vcf_map_samples(samples(hdr), samples):samples not in file: ‘C57BL_6J’

#Plot Assocition map with SDP
assoc.plot(results = results, thr = 5, show.sdps = TRUE)

#To add genes dowload the following files from jax: ftp://ftp.jax.org/SNPtools/genes/MGI.sorted.txt.gz.tbi and ftp://ftp.jax.org/SNPtools/genes/MGI.sorted.txt.gz
assoc.plot(results = results, mgi.file = "~/DO/MGI.sorted.txt.gz", thr = 5, show.sdps = TRUE)

Jessica Mayeux

My guess is that the map object doesn't correspond to the genoprobs object. The function index_snps() is using the map object to figure out which marker interval each SNP sits in, but then it's saying that index_snps() has given marker intervals that are outside the range of the number of possible intervals in genoprobs.

These two vectors of numbers should be identical:

  sapply(map, length)
  sapply(genoprobs, function(a) dim(a)[3])

karl

This is a little off topic for my original question, but since you mentioned your frustration with the current iteration of MQM in rqtl, may I ask a quick question about that?

For our data the Multiple-QTL Mapping approach would really be better, as we believe we have quite a few QTL per chromosome in some cases. One thing that is odd, however, is that the MQM model that is generated by mqmscan does not seem to match up well with the lod profile in the plot output. Specifically, in some cases the model will indicate that there are two QTL next to each other, but the lod profile will look like one peak with a lod max somewhere between the two. Do you know why that may be happening? I have not been able to find any other examples like this.

All the best,

Eden
